'''''Dicksonia fibrosa''''', the '''golden tree fern''', {{lang|mi|whekī-ponga}}, {{lang|mi|wheki-kōnga}},<ref name="nzpcn">{{cite web |title=Dicksonia fibrosa |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/dicksonia-fibrosa/ |website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |access-date=18 October 2024 }}</ref> or {{lang|mi|kurīpākā}} (in [[Māori language|Māori]]) is a [[species]] of medium-sized [[Cyatheales|tree fern]] [[native plant|native]] to New Zealand. It is similar to the related ''[[Dicksonia antarctica]]'' in that it is slow-growing and can withstand sub-zero temperatures.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Brock |first1=James M. R. |last2=Bellvé |first2=André M. |last3=Burns |first3=Bruce R. |date=2025 |title=Marcescence and prostrate growth in tree ferns are adaptations to cold tolerance |journal=Ecography |language=en |volume=2025 |issue=6 |article-number=e07362 |doi=10.1111/ecog.07362 |issn=1600-0587|doi-access=free |hdl=2292/71595 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>



==Etymology and taxonomy==
{{lang|la|Dicksonia fibrosa}} Colenso in Hooker, ''Sp. Fil.'' 1, 68 (1844) was originally collected by [[William Colenso|Colenso]], but was inadvertently described by [[Joseph Dalton Hooker|Hooker]].<ref name="nzflora" /> ''Dicksonia'' refers to [[James Dickson (botanist)|James Dickson]]. {{lang|la|fibrosa}} refers to the fibrous trunk.<ref name="nzpcn" /> 

{{lang|la|D. fibrosa}} is known by the names {{lang|mi|kuranui-pākā}}, {{lang|mi|kurīpākā}}, {{lang|mi|pūnui}}, {{lang|mi|tūkirunga}}, {{lang|mi|wekī}}, {{lang|mi|whekī}}, {{lang|mi|wheki-ponga}}, {{lang|mi|whekī-kōhunga}}, {{lang|mi|wheki-kohoonga}}, or {{lang|mi|whekī-ponga}} in [[Māori language|Māori]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Brock |first1=James M. R. |last2=Perry |first2=George L. W. |last3=Lee |first3=William G. |last4=Burns |first4=Bruce R. |date=1 September 2016 |title=Tree fern ecology in New Zealand: A model for southern temperate rainforests |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0378112716302705 |journal=Forest Ecology and Management |volume=375 |pages=112–126 |doi=10.1016/j.foreco.2016.05.030 |issn=0378-1127 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Description==

{{lang|la|D. fibrosa}} has a thick, soft and fibrous rusty brown trunk. According to Large & Braggins, the trunk can be up to {{convert|2|m|0}} in diameter.<ref name=":1">{{cite book |last1=Large |first1=Mark F. |last2=Braggins |first2=John E. |date=2004 |title=Tree Ferns |location=Portland, Oregon |publisher=Timber Press |pages=20, 284 & 288 }}</ref> It holds on to its dead leaves producing a distinctive pale brown skirt, distinguishing it from the related {{lang|la|[[Dicksonia squarrosa]]}}.<ref name="Native Ferns">{{cite book |title=A Guide to the Identification of New Zealand Native Ferns |last=Andrew Crowe |year=1997 |page=11 |publisher=Penguin Books |location=Auckland, New Zealand }}</ref> A slow-growing plant, similar to {{lang|la|[[Dicksonia antarctica]]}},<ref name="Dicksonia antarctica comparison">{{cite web |url=http://www.forestferns.co.uk/tree-ferns/dicksonia/dicksonia-fibrosa |title=Dicksonia antarctica comparison }}</ref> {{lang|la|D. fibrosa}} can reach a height of {{convert|6|m|0}}. It requires winter protection in any area that is subject to winter frosts. A local race or variety of ''D. fibrosa'' found to the region of [[Tauranga]] regularly branches [[dichotomous]]ly producing as many as nineteen forks.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dobbie |first=H. B. |date=April–June 1929 |title=A Forest of Forked Tree Ferns |journal=American Fern Journal |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=41–44 |doi=10.2307/1543717 |jstor=1543717 }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''D. fibrosa'' can be found in the South Island, Chatham Islands, and in the North Island, but is uncommon north of the Waikato River and Coromandel Peninsula.<ref name="nzpcn" /> It is rare on Stewart Island.<ref name="nzflora">{{cite web |title=Flora of New Zealand {{!}} Taxon Profile {{!}} Dicksonia fibrosa |url=https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/Taxon/Dicksonia-fibrosa.html|website=Flora of New Zealand |access-date=18 October 2024 }}</ref>

It is now naturalised in the Auckland area, and on Hawaiʻi.<ref name="nzflora" />

''D. fibrosa'' inhabits coastal and montane areas. It extends up to 1100 m in elevation in [[Kaweka Range|Kaweka]] and [[Ruahine range|Ruahine]] ranges of the North Island, but only to around 400 m in Marlborough.<ref name="nzflora" />

''D. fibrosa'' prefers wet areas and gulleys, under full forest cover, particularly [[Podocarpaceae|podocarp]], [[Nothofagus|southern beech]] or broadleaf forests.<ref name="nzflora" /><ref name="nzpcn" />

It is quite cold-hardy and can be found in many temperate regions that experience sub-zero temperatures.<ref name=":2" />

==Ecology==
{{lang|la|D. fibrosa}} is a long-lived species, up to 250 years. They are important for nutrient cycling, as well as for influencing the light locally where they can shade-out light-loving species. Their stems can also provide locations for epiphytes.<ref name=":0" /> The species is also a host for many species of fungi.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 May 2011 |title=Dicksonia fibrosa Colenso |url=https://biotanz.landcareresearch.co.nz/scientific-names/cd97a2e2-db4b-40dd-ae2a-b1dc6dc61cdd |access-date=19 October 2024 |website=Biota of NZ }}</ref>

Slabs cut from the thick stem of the whekī-ponga, alongside ''D. squarrosa'', were used by [[Māori people|Māori]] over 150 years ago in constructing the outside of houses, or lining underground storage spaces.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dicksonia fibrosa. Whekī-ponga. Tree fern. |url=https://rauropiwhakaoranga.landcareresearch.co.nz/names/f286833a-d718-4dd1-a622-1ae438f3350d |website=rauropiwhakaoranga.landcareresearch.co.nz |publisher=Manaaki Whenua Landcare Research |access-date=14 February 2023 }}</ref>

It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Dicksonia fibrosa'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5796/Dicksonia-fibrosa/Details |access-date=27 May 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=29 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=6 February 2018 |quote=Other common names; woolly tree fern. Synonyms; ''Cyathea fibrosa'' }}</ref>
